e-4725.knowledge_point: Transforming a 2x2 Matrix Into the Identity Matrix Using Row Operations
e-4725.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2 \,$ and $\, R_2 :=  R_2+(-1)R_1?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14080619/assets/e607bba88cc1f15abaa45fc3cf02110243433d60259c56805515ced373054ca0.png)
e-4725.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

e-4724.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
e-4724.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine $A^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
e-4724.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix $A^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

e-4723.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
e-4723.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
e-4723.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
R_1 := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1,
\qquad
R_1 := R_1+(-3)R_2.
$$

The matrix $A^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

content.knowledge_point: Transforming a 2x2 Matrix Into the Identity Matrix Using Row Operations
content.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 6

The inverse of the 2×2 matrix A is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine A−1.

[A|I]=[10103−101]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[10100−1−31]R2:=___________∼[10aa01aa]

a
A−1=[1013]
b
A−1=[103−1]
c
A−1=[1−13−1]
d
A−1=[1031]
e
A−1=[1−1130]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We write down A and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix A into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[A|I]=[10103−101]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[10100−1−31]R2:=(−1)R2∼[1010013−1]

The matrix A−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, A−1=[103−1].

verification.explanation: The final operation is R₂ := −R₂, yielding the augmented row (0,1 | 3,−1). The right-hand block is therefore A⁻¹ = [[1,0],[3,−1]], confirming the revealed solution and the earlier answer.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 7

The inverse of the 2×2 matrix A is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine A−1.

[A|I]=[1310−2−501]R2:=R2+2R1∼[13100121]R1:=___________∼[10aa01aa]

a
A−1=[−5321]
b
A−1=[−53−21]
c
A−1=[5−32−1]
d
A−1=[−5−321]
e
A−1=[2153]
Submit

decision.explanation: Use R₁ := R₁ − 3R₂. The first right-hand row becomes (1,0) − 3(2,1) = (−5,−3), while the second remains (2,1). Thus A⁻¹ = [[−5,−3],[2,1]].

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 7
?

The inverse of the 2×2 matrix A is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine A−1.

[A|I]=[1310−2−501]R2:=R2+2R1∼[13100121]R1:=___________∼[10aa01aa]

a
A−1=[−5321]
b
A−1=[−53−21]
c
A−1=[5−32−1]
d
A−1=[−5−321]
e
A−1=[2153]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We write down A and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix A into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[A|I]=[1310−2−501]R2:=R2+2R1∼[13100121]R1:=R1+(−3)R2∼[10−5−30121]

The matrix A−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, A−1=[−5−321].

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $B$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${B}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $B$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${B}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

[B|I]=[10103501]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[101005−31]R2:=___________∼[10aa01aa]

a
 B−1=[103515]
b
B−1=[10−3515]
c
B−1=[1−135−15]
d
B−1=[13−3515]
e
B−1=[1035−15]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We write down B and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix B into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[B|I]=[10103501]R2:=R2+(−3)R1∼[101005−31]R2:=15R2∼[101001−3515]

The matrix B−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

B−1=[10−3515].

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $B$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${B}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $B$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${B}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Complete the process with R₁ := R₁ − 2R₂. On the right-hand side, (0,1) − 2(1,2) = (−2,−3), while the second row remains (1,2). Thus E⁻¹ = [[−2,−3],[1,2]].

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $E$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${E}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[E\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $E$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $E$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[E\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${E}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{E}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

We write down E and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix E into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $E$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${E}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[E\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $E$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $E$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[E\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${E}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{E}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 11
?

The inverse of the matrix A is found using the row operations as shown below. What are the corresponding row operations?

[A|I]=[11102301]___________∼[111001−21]___________∼[103−101−21]

a
R1:=R1+(−2)R2,R2:=−R2
b
R2:=R2+(−1)R2,R1:=R2+R2
c
R1:=R1+(−2)R2,R2:=R2+R1
d
R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+(−1)R2
e
R2:=R2+(−1)R2,R1:=−2R2
Submit

decision.explanation: First, R₂ − 2R₁ = (0,1,−2,1). Then R₁ − R₂ = (1,0,3,−1), using the updated second row. These are exactly the two displayed transitions.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using the row operations as shown below. What are the corresponding row operations?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 11
?

The inverse of the matrix A is found using the row operations as shown below. What are the corresponding row operations?

[A|I]=[11102301]___________∼[111001−21]___________∼[103−101−21]

a
R1:=R1+(−2)R2,R2:=−R2
b
R2:=R2+(−1)R2,R1:=R2+R2
c
R1:=R1+(−2)R2,R2:=R2+R1
d
R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+(−1)R2
e
R2:=R2+(−1)R2,R1:=−2R2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We write down A and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix A into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[A|I]=[11102301]R2:=R2+(−2)R1∼[111001−21]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[103−101−21]

The corresponding row operations are

R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+(−1)R2.

The matrix A−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

A−1=[3−1−21]

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using the row operations as shown below. What are the corresponding row operations?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

?

[K|I]=[−3410−2301]R1:=−13R1∼[1−43−130−2301]___________∼[1−43−130013−231]R2:=3R2∼[1−43−13001−23]___________∼[10−3401−23]

a
R2:=R2+(−2)R1,R1:=R1+34R2
b
R2:=R2+(−1)R1,R1:=R1+(−3)R2
c
R2:=R2+12R1,R1:=R1+13R2

decision.explanation: The first blank is R₂ := R₂ + 2R₁, giving (0,1/3,−2/3,1). After scaling R₂ by 3, use R₁ := R₁ + (4/3)R₂, giving (1,0,−3,4). Both transitions match the displayed matrices.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $K$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[K\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $K$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $K$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[K\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+\frac{4}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{4}{3}{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${K}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{K}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $K$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[K\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $K$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $K$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[K\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{4}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+\frac{4}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{4}{3}{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${K}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{K}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

[V|I]=[11100201]___________∼[111001012]___________∼[101−1201012]

a
R2:=12R2,R1:=R1+(−1)R2
b
R2:=14R2,R1:=R1+2R2
c
R2:=32R2,R1:=R1+(−3)R2
d
R2:=2R2,R1:=R1+R2
e

decision.explanation: First halve R₂, changing (0,2,0,1) to (0,1,0,1/2). Then subtract the updated R₂ from R₁, giving (1,0,1,−1/2). These match both displayed steps.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $V$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $V$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $V$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${V}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{V}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 13
?

The inverse of the matrix V is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

[V|I]=[11100201]___________∼[111001012]___________∼[101−1201012]

a
R2:=12R2,R1:=R1+(−1)R2
b
R2:=14R2,R1:=R1+2R2
c
R2:=32R2,R1:=R1+(−3)R2
d
R2:=2R2,R1:=R1+R2
e
R1:=12R1,R2:=R2+(−1)R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We write down V and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix V into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[V|I]=[11100201]R2:=12R2∼[111001012]R1:=R1+(−1)R2∼[101−1201012]

The corresponding row operations are R2:=12R2,R1:=R1+(−1)R2.

The matrix V−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

V−1=[1−12012].

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $V$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $V$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $V$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[V\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-1){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${V}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{V}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Divide R₂ by 3 to obtain (0,1,0,1/3). Then add (5/2)R₂ to R₁, eliminating −5/2 and producing the final entry (5/2)(1/3) = 5/6. Both steps match the displayed matrices.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $J$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[J\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{6} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $J$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $J$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[J\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{6} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${J}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{J}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{6} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

We write down J and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix J into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[J|I]=[2−5100301]R1:=12R1∼[1−521200301]R2:=13R2∼[1−5212001013]R1:=R1+52R2∼[10125601013]

The corresponding row operations are R1:=12R1,R2:=13R2,R1:=R1+52R2.

The matrix J−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

J−1=[1256013].

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $J$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[J\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{6} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $J$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $J$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[J\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{5}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{6} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${J}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{J}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & \frac{5}{6} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Multiply R₂ by −2/3 to change (0,−3/2,1/2,1) into (0,1,−1/3,−2/3). Then subtract half of R₂ from R₁, giving (1,0,2/3,1/3). These match both displayed transitions.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${Y}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Y}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

content.knowledge_point: Determining the Row Operations Required To Find the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $Y$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to the blank spaces?

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${Y}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Y}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
